A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, and the methods, equations, results, and relocated sections can be reliably matched.

before.justification: V1 reports original representation analyses, including four-model similarity results in Table 1, heatmaps in Figures 2–5, and MATH500 trajectory visualizations.

after.justification: V2 retains those original results and adds two model evaluations, a shuffled-step control, and a velocity-norm diagnostic in Figure 6.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, cumulative-context representations, final-layer mean pooling, and the velocity/curvature analysis remain unchanged. The new controls and explanatory qualifications do not revise the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: V2 adds randomly reordered logical sequences as a perturbed-input scenario. The 30 logical structures, 20 topics, four languages, 2,430 sequences, and selected MATH500 example are retained. Japanese was already included in v1 Section 5.2.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds an explicitly evaluated Random Shuffle baseline using Qwen3 0.6B, comparing shuffled and intact reasoning sequences. The additional Qwen models are applications of the same analysis, rather than competing reasoning-analysis methods.

E3.justification: V2 adds Qwen1.5 0.5B and Qwen2 0.5B configurations, a sentence-order permutation control, and a finite-difference velocity-norm diagnostic for six existing MATH500 answers. The original extraction, pooling, grouping, and similarity metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds an order-destruction ablation testing whether higher-order similarities depend on reasoning sequence, plus Appendix B's smoothness diagnostic addressing Hypothesis 4.6. These substantially expand checks on two central interpretations; v1's existing model-size and family heatmaps are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for these experiments. V2 retains the existing aggregation practice and supplies no uncertainty estimates for the shuffle control or continuity diagnostic.

E6.justification: All four original Table 1 rows and existing heatmaps are unchanged. V2 adds two Qwen rows, shuffle results, and Figure 6. Shuffled Qwen3 0.6B inputs yield logic-group velocity/curvature similarities of 0.02/0.02, compared with 0.17/0.53 for intact inputs: a new control finding, not a same-setting performance change.

T1.justification: The formal hypotheses, alignment corollary, integrated-velocity proposition, relaxed-mask proof, and curvature derivations are retained. New Remark 4.8 explains the already domain-restricted injectivity assumption; notation corrections and this clarification do not introduce different mathematical results.

C1.justification: Both versions claim logic-sensitive reasoning geometry. V2's abstract and introduction additionally foreground next-token-only learning and a general, possibly universal representational law independent of training recipes or architectures. This substantially broadens the claimed scientific scope, although the original contribution bullets and conclusion remain.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly restricts the framework to post-hoc understanding, excluding generation accuracy and training dynamics. It clarifies that logical constraints are not explicit inference-rule operators and that finite trajectory diagnostics cannot verify C1 regularity. It also adds interpretations connecting order sensitivity and cross-model consistency to compression and universal representations.

D1.justification: V2 documents sentence-level permutation before Qwen3 0.6B encoding and specifies consecutive-state differences and their norms for the new diagnostic. Existing pooling details, GPT-5 generation prompts, and code/data access links are retained; no shuffle seeds or additional implementation specifications are supplied.

R1.justification: V2 adds substantive comparisons with Park et al. (2025) and Li et al. (2025a), distinguishing dynamic reasoning from static semantics and training dynamics. New connections to the Platonic Representation Hypothesis, compression, and the meaning-versus-form debate substantially expand positioning. Existing mechanistic-interpretability and formal-logic discussions are relocated, not removed.

P1.justification: V2 locally expands the abstract and discussion, introduces paragraph headings in Sections 4.3 and 6.2, moves two related-work discussions into Appendix A, and changes citation style. The core eight-section progression and much of the original prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Document-wide conversion to the ICLR format changes margins, typography, title and abstract layout, headers, and figure/table placement. Table 1 expands and a velocity-norm Figure 6 is added. Existing heatmaps and curvature illustrations are preserved, with the latter renumbered Figures 7–8.

improvement.justification: The shuffle control adds useful evidence about order sensitivity, and the additional model results modestly strengthen replication. Explicit scope boundaries and acknowledgment that the continuity diagnostic cannot prove smoothness improve interpretability. These gains are limited by stronger next-token-only and universality claims that the added experiments do not establish.
